page: Google Cloud Platform n4a-highmem-4 is an arm64-based virtual machine instance belonging to the n4a server family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached block storage. Additionally, it does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

From a resource density perspective, the n4a-highmem-4 offers a high memory allocation relative to its compute capacity. This memory-optimized profile provides qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring substantial memory footprints without the need for high vCPU counts. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU accelerators represents a clear tradeoff, limiting its utility for high-throughput local I/O operations or hardware-accelerated parallel processing.

The architectural profile of this instance makes it suitable for memory-intensive workloads that run efficiently on the arm64 architecture. Typical use cases include medium-sized databases, in-memory caching layers, enterprise applications with moderate CPU demands, and lightweight data processing pipelines.
